_doc: EoX (end-of-x) records for every environment this repo builds and measures on (#376): hosted runner images, the operating systems under them, and the pinned Rust channel. Each product's lifecycle statement is an OpenEoX Core v1.0 document (OASIS OpenEoX TC) embedded verbatim under `eox`, validated by `cargo xtask eox-check` against the schema copy pinned in SCHEMA.lock to the conformance clause 'EoX Core Information' (schema + section 7.1 mandatory tests). OpenEoX Core carries only the dated transition events; product identification is delegated to a surrounding schema by design (CSD01 section 4.1.4), which is what the fields beside `eox` are.

Vendor-announced dates only inside `eox`: a date the vendor has not published is `tba`, never an estimate. Estimates live in `projection`, labelled as such, with the pattern they rest on; a projection reaching the warning window is itself a finding ('confirm or correct'), and one reaching the failure window fails until a reviewed record replaces it.

`end_of_active_support` is the date a hosted runner image enters deprecation (brownouts begin; GitHub says deprecation, endoflife.date says end of active support). OpenEoX Core v1.0 has no event for it, so it sits beside `eox` as a shell field. A runner image has no security-only phase: `end_of_security_support` equals `end_of_life` (removal).

Operating-system records (kind `os`) map Canonical's standard security maintenance end to `end_of_security_support` and Expanded Security Maintenance end (Ubuntu Pro) to `end_of_life`; the paid Legacy add-on beyond ESM is not counted as vendor support here.

`crosscheck.endoflife` names the endoflife.date v1 API release the record is compared against in the weekly monitor (releaseDate ~ general_availability, eoasFrom ~ end_of_active_support, eolFrom / eoesFrom ~ the mapped end fields, null ~ tba). A mismatch FAILS (the record is stale or wrong); an unreachable source is a loud warning and never a pass.

Enforcement windows (`thresholds_days`): for every `runs-on` label a workflow uses, FAIL when the announced or projected end_of_active_support is within `fail` days (or has passed), WARN within `warn` days. Brownouts precede removal, so the clock runs to deprecation start, not to end_of_life. Dates are UTC calendar dates.

one_image_rules._doc: Every Linux job that consumes cargo-acl (cackle) builds and measures on ONE image: the glibc floor and bwrap behavior are properties of the image, and a caps inventory measured on a different image than the producer built on is not a measurement of the producer's bytes (#381 fidelity note).

products.note: Not used by any workflow since 2026-11-09; kept as the record of the miss that motivated #376 (deprecation began 2026-09-17, brownouts 2027-03-23..04-13 14:00-00:00 UTC, removal 2027-04-17).

projection.basis: Pattern of the two retired LTS images: removal ~6.5 weeks before Canonical's standard-support end (20.04: OS 2025-05-31 -> image removed 2025-04-15; 22.04: OS 2027-06-01 -> removed 2027-04-17); deprecation start 3 months (20.04) to 7 months (22.04) before removal, the earlier figure is used. 24.04 OS standard support ends 2029-05-31.
Same pattern as ubuntu-24.04; 26.04 OS standard support ends 2031-05-29. GA 2026-09-17 (actions/runner-images#14747); ubuntu-latest moved to it 2026-10-19..11-19 (#14748).

products.note: No projection: GitHub retires a Windows image once two newer exist (windows-2019 retired 2025-06-30 after 2022 and 2025 shipped); no windows-2028 image is announced, so there is no pattern date to project from. The weekly cross-check is what catches the announcement.

rust-lang publishes no EoX for a channel: only the current stable, beta and nightly are supported, so a pinned nightly is unsupported the day the next one ships. The record exists so the pin is tracked as data; the operative control is the age proxy in the monitor (warn past 75 days) and the 30-day soak in TOOLCHAIN.lock. eox-check requires this id to match the lock's channel, so a toolchain bump must touch this record.
